note: Paths are values read from the records. A surface is computed from two paths and is not a measurement. Simulated magnitudes are for comparing actuators, not forecasts of hardware. Lengths in metres, angles in radians.

quantities.label: Axial tip travel
quantities.definition: Tip displacement from rest along the record's x axis, the base-to-tip axis, as stored in free.tip_displacement_m. Positive is the tip moving away from the base.

quantities.label: Bending tip travel
quantities.definition: Length of the sideways part of the stored tip displacement: the square root of (y squared plus z squared). Measured from rest, like the stored displacement, not from the first measured level.

quantities.label: Tip twist
quantities.definition: Rotation of the tip about the record's x axis: the x component of the tip rotation vector stored in free.tip_rotvec, at each level. Null for the whole leg where the record holds no tip rotation: not measured, not zero.

quantities.label: Sideways travel, y
quantities.definition: Tip displacement from rest along the record's y axis, as stored in free.tip_displacement_m.

quantities.label: Sideways travel, z
quantities.definition: Tip displacement from rest along the record's z axis, as stored in free.tip_displacement_m.

quantities.label: Share of input range
quantities.definition: For each input channel, the size of its input divided by the largest size of input that channel takes anywhere in the record's free rows; the share is the largest of these over the channels. Every value lies between 0 and 1. For a single-input record it is the size of the input over the largest size in the leg: it rises along the leg, starts at 0 where the first input is zero and ends at exactly 1. On a leg with another channel held above zero it starts at that channel's share (0.5 for a chamber held at half its largest pressure) and stays there until the leg's own input passes it. Works the same way for vacuum (negative) inputs.

quantities.label: Bend angle (estimate)
quantities.group: Body shape, estimated from the tip position
quantities.definition: Estimated from the tip position and the body length: twice the angle at the base between the x axis and the straight line from the base to the tip. It assumes the body is one even arc from the base to the tip, with the tip at rest a body length along the x axis. It is exact for such a body, reads zero bend for a body that only extends, and is wrong for a body that bends in only part of its length (on the two tandem twist drafts, which bend in two parts, it does not match the tilt of the tip measured from the stored tip rotation). The bend lies between 0 and 360 degrees, so a body curling past a full turn is not represented. No estimate where the tip is closer to the base than 30% of the body length, because there the tip's direction no longer says how far the body has bent. Null for the whole leg where the actuator has no length: not measured, not zero.

quantities.label: Stretch (estimate)
quantities.group: Body shape, estimated from the tip position
quantities.definition: Estimated from the tip position and the body length: the length of the even arc from the base to the tip, divided by the body length, less 1. Positive is the body longer than at rest. It depends strongly on the body length for a body that bends a lot; each leg says how far it moves when the length is changed by 5% either way. It assumes the body is one even arc from the base to the tip, with the tip at rest a body length along the x axis. It is exact for such a body, reads zero bend for a body that only extends, and is wrong for a body that bends in only part of its length (on the two tandem twist drafts, which bend in two parts, it does not match the tilt of the tip measured from the stored tip rotation). The bend lies between 0 and 360 degrees, so a body curling past a full turn is not represented. No estimate where the tip is closer to the base than 30% of the body length, because there the tip's direction no longer says how far the body has bent. Null for the whole leg where the actuator has no length: not measured, not zero.

quantities.label: Bend toward y (estimate)
quantities.group: Body shape, estimated from the tip position
quantities.definition: The estimated bend angle times the share of the sideways tip travel that lies along the record's y axis (y travel over sideways travel); 0 where the tip has not moved sideways. It assumes the body is one even arc from the base to the tip, with the tip at rest a body length along the x axis. It is exact for such a body, reads zero bend for a body that only extends, and is wrong for a body that bends in only part of its length (on the two tandem twist drafts, which bend in two parts, it does not match the tilt of the tip measured from the stored tip rotation). The bend lies between 0 and 360 degrees, so a body curling past a full turn is not represented. No estimate where the tip is closer to the base than 30% of the body length, because there the tip's direction no longer says how far the body has bent. Null for the whole leg where the actuator has no length: not measured, not zero.

quantities.label: Bend toward z (estimate)
quantities.group: Body shape, estimated from the tip position
quantities.definition: The estimated bend angle times the share of the sideways tip travel that lies along the record's z axis (z travel over sideways travel); 0 where the tip has not moved sideways. It assumes the body is one even arc from the base to the tip, with the tip at rest a body length along the x axis. It is exact for such a body, reads zero bend for a body that only extends, and is wrong for a body that bends in only part of its length (on the two tandem twist drafts, which bend in two parts, it does not match the tilt of the tip measured from the stored tip rotation). The bend lies between 0 and 360 degrees, so a body curling past a full turn is not represented. No estimate where the tip is closer to the base than 30% of the body length, because there the tip's direction no longer says how far the body has bent. Null for the whole leg where the actuator has no length: not measured, not zero.

quantities.label: Axial tip travel ÷ length
quantities.group: Tip travel as a share of length
quantities.definition: Axial tip travel divided by the body length. A body that bends also brings its tip back toward the base, so a negative value does not by itself mean the body got shorter. Null for the whole leg where the actuator has no length: not measured, not zero.

quantities.label: Sideways tip travel ÷ length
quantities.group: Tip travel as a share of length
quantities.definition: Bending tip travel (the length of the sideways part of the tip displacement) divided by the body length. Null for the whole leg where the actuator has no length: not measured, not zero.

task_cones.half_angle_basis: A choice made for the display, not a limit measured on the task. Inside 45 degrees the tip has moved further along the needed direction than across it (the squared cosine is above one half). The task file gives no angle. The range of angles for which the records inside the cone are exactly the stored turners is worked out by tests/test_export_map_paths.py and is not used to choose this number.
task_cones.least_travel_note: The task file states no least tip travel, so the cone has no floor: any travel inside the angle counts. Its far end is one stroke of the wave.

stroke.basis: The stroke angle is the wave's commanded sweep of each fingertip about the turn axis during contact, read from the same run command the task file takes its duty from. That run only settled the ball, so this is the commanded stroke, not a measured turn of the ball. The tip travel for one stroke is the stroke angle times the contact ring's distance from the turn axis (ball radius times the cosine of the ring altitude, both from the task file), the inverse of the repository's own turn-per-stroke rule (gramian_workshop.arrange.Arrangement.turn_per_stroke_deg). Here the stroke may start from any tip position the finger holds, not only from rest: see return_clear.stroke_from_basis. The tip's real target is an arc about the turn axis; the straight cone with a far end is a simplification.

return_clear.basis: After each stroke the finger must let go of the ball and come back to where the stroke began without dragging the ball back with it. So the return path must sit further out of the ball than the stroke path, at every travel along the stroke: less travel along the contact normal, which points into the ball. This is read from free tip positions only; nothing here simulates the ball, or the push on it. Distance from the ball's curved surface is not used, because the stroke is drawn straight and a straight path leaves a ball by geometry alone. A finger with one input has one tip position at each travel, so it can only come back the way it went.
return_clear.drawn_depth_basis: A choice made for the display, not a clearance measured on the task. The task file states none. tests/test_export_map_paths.py checks that, on the records held under this declaration, every pass or fail is the same for any depth from a hundredth of a millimetre up to 7 mm.
return_clear.stroke_from_basis: On this placement the finger stands beside the ball, and a second input can carry its tip towards the ball or away from it. So the stroke need not start at rest: the finger may first bring its tip onto the ball with one input, then stroke with the other. The stroke path is therefore any line of held tip positions, judged from its own start. The finger's base is taken to be set back so that the tip meets the ball where that line starts; that moves the finger without turning it, so the needed direction and the contact normal are the same. Moving between the stroke line and the return line, at the two ends of the stroke, is a change of the held input and is not checked.

task_cones.name: Turn a ball in a cup (make/break wave)

force_note: Force with the tip held, read from the record's blocked block, at the input levels that block holds and no others. Most simulated records hold the tip at its rest position; some published ones hold it elsewhere, and each actuator's own method text says how. So this is the force at one held pose, not along the tip path. Axial force is signed as stored, along the base-to-tip axis. Where the record holds the whole force vector its direction is known; where it holds only the size of the sideways part, the direction of that part about the axis is not known. A part the record does not hold is null: not measured, not zero. Moments are about the inlet centroid. The simulated forces were read before the body had fully settled, so they are comparative, not predictive.

scaled.note: Quantities with size and material taken out. For one geometry the shape depends only on the input over the body's stiffness, and at the same shape the force grows with E times L squared (E: Young's modulus of the body; L: body length). So tip travel over L, the scaled input, and force over E L squared let actuators of different size and material be compared. Axial and sideways tip travel over L are the quantities axial_share and bending_share in the main list; they are not repeated here. The scaled input mixes forms: a pressure over E, a cable tension over E L squared, or a cable pull over L; each leg says which. A simulated pressure is first corrected as data/map_pressure_scale.json says, for the records it lists; that correction has not been ruled on. Simulated magnitudes are comparative, not predictive.

quantities.label: Input, scaled
quantities.definition: The leg's own input made into a pure number with the body's stiffness and length, in the form that suits the kind of input: a pressure over the body's Young's modulus E; a cable tension over E times the body length squared; a cable pull (a length) over the body length, which needs no stiffness. The axis mixes these forms, and each leg names its own (input_scaled_form) and spells out its rule (input_scaled_definition). A simulated pressure is first multiplied by the correction data/map_pressure_scale.json lists for that record (1 / dt for the scene's pressure, which has not been ruled on); a published pressure is used as stated. On a leg with another input held, only the leg's own input is scaled. Null for the whole leg where the form needs a modulus or a length the actuator does not have, or the input is of a kind with no rule; each leg says why.

scene_pressure.why: In the simulation scene the pressure constraint takes its value as an impulse over one time step, so the scene's 'Pa' is 1 / dt smaller than a physical pascal: 100 times at the scene's time step of 0.01 s. A clamped bar loaded once by gravity and once by the pressure constraint, at two time steps, shows it: the ratio of the two sags follows 0.01 / dt to within about 1.2%. That check is on a bar built with the same SOFA components, not on the actuator scenes themselves. Not yet ruled on by the project owner.
scene_pressure.dt_note: The scene's time step as committed. The sweep runners accept --dt and the records do not state the step each run used, so the factor rests on the scene default.
scene_pressure.chosen_by: Every record and draft record whose source.kind is simulation, whose provenance.scene is parametricGripper.py, and which has an input channel in Pa.
